root_cause.text: The mac80211 TTLM parsing function unconditionally reads a link map presence indicator byte, even when the control flags indicate a default link map where that byte is absent, resulting in an out-of-bounds read one byte beyond the element.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a conditional check `if (!(control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP))` before reading the `link_map_presence` byte, and the CVE description explicitly states that "mac80211 would incorrectly parse the frame and would also read one byte beyond the end of the element."

intent_record.what: Changed the copyright year from 2025 to 2026 in the Intel Corporation copyright notice in the file header.
intent_record.how: This updates the copyright end year in the comment block; no behavioral or functional change to the code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix parsing of T2L advertisement by skipping the link_map_presence field when the default link map control flag is set.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check (if (!(control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP))) around the assignment of link_map_presence and the advancement of pos pointer.
intent_record.how: The change causes the link_map_presence byte to be read only when the control flag IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP is not set. If the flag is set, the byte is skipped, preventing incorrect parsing.

grouping_result.intent: Fix parsing of T2L advertisement by skipping the link_map_presence field when the default link map control flag is set.

relevance_review.reason: The group only updates the copyright year to 2026, which is a non-functional, administrative change with no connection to the out-of-bounds read vulnerability in TTLM parsing.
The group explicitly addresses the root cause by fixing the parsing logic to skip the link_map_presence field when the default link map control flag is set, preventing the out-of-bounds read.
